describes: What the pull-request reviewer (`.github/workflows/pr-review.yml`, deciding through `scripts/pr-review.mjs`) reads to decide a merge: the shape of an issue's ID in a title, the status context it sets and the check it waits for, its labels and who may apply the approval one, which rubric the branch reviewer holds each path to, which paths and JSON keys make a pull request high risk, and how it merges.
whyThisFileExists: The reviewer decides by every value here, so a pull request that changed one could lower its own bar. `prReviewHighRiskPaths` names this file, so a person merges every change to it (`docs/decisions.md` § D-07 and § D-27). Before D-27 these keys shared `tools/policy.json` with the rest of the policy and were made high risk key by key, through `prReviewHighRiskJsonKeys`, because that whole file was too wide; in a record of their own they are held whole, by path.
gatedBy: mise run check:policy holds this record's header, a `Means` beside every constant, and no key another record also defines. mise run pr-review:check holds the `prReview*` keys: it refuses a missing key or `Means` sibling, a value of the wrong shape, a policy whose `prReviewHighRiskPaths` does not cover the reviewer's own files, the branch reviewer, the approval-label guard and the helper it imports, this record, `tools/policy/prompt-budgets.json`, the loader the reviewer reads them through, `tools/lib/policy.ts`, the git helper the job that merges imports, `tools/lib/git-env.ts`, or the toolchain (`docs/decisions.md` § D-31): `mise.toml`, `mise.lock`, a nested `mise.toml`, a `mise.local.toml`, a `.mise/` directory and `.devcontainer/Dockerfile`; a `.github/workflows/pr-review.yml` or `.github/workflows/verify.yml` that spells a label, a status context or a check other than the policy does; and a `pr-review.yml` whose jobs run anything their allowlist leaves out, a language model, a package in the job that merges or a command of a step's own among it, or that reads a secret however spelt, mints an OIDC token, `write-all` included, interpolates an expression into a shell, or gives the job that computes the evidence no read-only token of its own (`docs/decisions.md` § D-37); mise run pr-review:selftest runs the reviewer's decisions over fixtures built from these values, and each refusal over a doctored copy; and mise run worktree:selftest holds `prReviewLabels.approved` as `scripts/hooks/guard-git.mjs` reads it, with a doctored respelling and a missing policy. mise run calculator:test and mise run trace:check read `prReviewIssuePattern` as the shape of a task's ID, through scripts/test-trace.mjs. mise run coupling:check reads `prReviewMergeMethod`, and refuses a merge method other than `rebase`.
whatItDoesNOTDo: The rubrics a branch is held to before its push are the prose of `.claude/agents/branch-reviewer.md`, and how the floor becomes a merge is `scripts/pr-review.mjs`; this file holds only the values both read. It holds no prompt's word budget, which a person also merges: that is `tools/policy/prompt-budgets.json`, which `prReviewHighRiskPaths` names too.
provenance: Split out of `tools/policy.json` on 2026-10-02 by D-27 (asdlc-openspec-umg3), each key with its value and its `Means` as that file held them at 962358c (`git show 962358c:tools/policy.json`), except that `prReviewHighRiskPaths` gained this record, `tools/policy/prompt-budgets.json` and the loader, `tools/lib/policy.ts`, and `prReviewHighRiskJsonKeys` lost its entry for `tools/policy.json`, each `Means` saying why, and `prReviewContextPaths` names `tools/policy/**` where it named `tools/policy.json`. The `prReview*` keys came with D-07 (asdlc-openspec-mi6) on 2026-09-25. On 2026-10-04 D-37 (asdlc-openspec-qcqm) removed `prReviewBlockingSeverities` and the `changes` label when the reviewer stopped running a language model, and put `.claude/agents/branch-reviewer.md`, `scripts/hooks/guard-git.mjs` with the `scripts/hooks/_shared.mjs` it imports, and `tools/lib/git-env.ts` on the floor where `.claude/agents/pr-reviewer.md` had been. Each key carries its date and its evidence in its `Means`.
prReviewIssuePatternMeans: A tracker issue id, as a regular expression without anchors: this tracker's prefix, the hash, and a child's dotted suffix (`asdlc-openspec-zgh.9`). The issues a pull request carries are the ids that match it inside the parentheses at the end of its title, and nowhere else: a body names follow-ups and related issues it does not carry. `scripts/pr-review.mjs brief --local` reads them so the branch reviewer holds the branch to their acceptance criteria, and the trace and test-inventory readers take it as the shape of a task's id. Since D-37 (asdlc-openspec-qcqm, 2026-10-04) the pull-request reviewer decides nothing by them: a title that cites none is decided by the floor like any other. Change it with the tracker's prefix. Decided 2026-09-25 (asdlc-openspec-mi6).
prReviewStatusContextMeans: The commit status the reviewer sets on a pull request's head commit: pending once the session that opened the pull request, or a person, marks the head with `scripts/pr-review.mjs mark` (no job has marked one since 2026-09-28, asdlc-openspec-08a), until the reviewer has judged that commit, then success, failure or error with the reason in its description. It is what `gh pr checks --watch` waits on, so an agent watching its own pull request (`.claude/skills/open-pr/SKILL.md` § 6) reads the review's outcome as it reads any check. A verdict that needs a person sets success, not pending, so no watcher waits on a person. Renaming it strands the pending status on every open pull request until its next push. Decided 2026-09-25 (asdlc-openspec-mi6).
prReviewRequiredCheckMeans: The check run that must have passed on a commit before the reviewer acts on it: the one job of `.github/workflows/verify.yml`, whose check run carries the job's name. On a pull request's head it gates the review, so no review is spent on a head CI has refused; on `main`'s head it gates every merge, so after a bad merge the reviewer stops merging until `main` is green again. `mise run pr-review:check` refuses a `verify.yml` with no job of this name and a `pr-review.yml` whose `workflow_run` does not name that workflow. Decided 2026-09-25 (asdlc-openspec-mi6).
prReviewLabelsMeans: The labels the reviewer reads and writes on a pull request, each key its role and each value its spelling. `human`: the head is on the high-risk floor, and a person decides. `approved`: a person approves the merge of the head commit the reviewer last judged. It counts only when a person with a permission in `prReviewApproverPermissions` applied it after that verdict, and an agent never applies it (`CLAUDE.md` § Git workflow). `scripts/hooks/guard-git.mjs` refuses a session's `gh` command that applies it and reads its spelling from here, so a rename moves the guard too (`docs/decisions.md` § R-01). The reviewer creates the two if they are missing. Renaming one means renaming it on the repository in the same change, and `mise run pr-review:check` refuses a `pr-review.yml` that filters on another spelling of `approved`. Decided 2026-09-25 (asdlc-openspec-mi6). A third role, `changes`, marked a failed dimension until D-37 (asdlc-openspec-qcqm, 2026-10-04); the reviewer judges no dimension now, so nothing applies it.
prReviewApproverPermissionsMeans: The repository permissions, as GitHub's collaborator-permission endpoint names them, of an account whose application of the approval label counts. A bot's never does. GitHub cannot tell a person from an agent acting with that person's credentials, which is `docs/decisions.md` § R-01. Decided 2026-09-25 (asdlc-openspec-mi6).
prReviewContextPathsMeans: The files held to the context-engineering rubric: what an agent reads to decide what to do, meaning the rules, the prompts, the documents, the specs and the constants they cite. Every other file is held to the product rubric. `*` matches within one directory, `**` across directories, and `**/` also matches none. A file is classed by its path at the branch's head, and the brief `scripts/pr-review.mjs brief --local` writes names each file's class, so the branch reviewer does not choose; since D-37 (asdlc-openspec-qcqm, 2026-10-04) no rubric is applied in CI. Decided 2026-09-25 (asdlc-openspec-mi6). `.beads/PRIME.md` added 2026-10-03 (asdlc-openspec-z5gy), with the file: it is the text `bd prime` puts into every session, so a prompt.

prReviewHighRiskPaths..github/**: the workflows: what runs with the repository's token and secrets, this reviewer among them
prReviewHighRiskPaths..claude/settings.json: the hooks every session runs, the guards among them
prReviewHighRiskPaths..claude/agents/branch-reviewer.md: the branch reviewer, the one review of correctness and maintainability
prReviewHighRiskPaths.scripts/hooks/guard-git.mjs: the guard that refuses a session's application of the approval label
prReviewHighRiskPaths.scripts/hooks/_shared.mjs: the helper that guard imports, through which a change could loosen what it refuses
prReviewHighRiskPaths.tools/lib/git-env.ts: the git helper the job that merges imports, with the token that merges
prReviewHighRiskPaths.AGENTS.md: the pointer another harness follows to those rules
prReviewHighRiskPaths..beads/PRIME.md: the text `bd prime` puts into every session at its start and before each compaction
prReviewHighRiskPaths.docs/decisions.md: a recorded decision, which is the maintainer's to make
prReviewHighRiskPaths.package-lock.json: the dependency tree every gate and the product run on
prReviewHighRiskPaths.**/mise.toml: the tool versions every gate, hook and session runs on, as `engines` and the dependencies are, and a nested config mise reads under its directory
prReviewHighRiskPaths.mise.lock: the download URL and checksum each of those tools is installed and verified from
prReviewHighRiskPaths.**/mise.*.toml: a mise config beside `mise.toml`, whose tools, settings, env or hooks mise loads with it
prReviewHighRiskPaths.**/.mise.toml: a mise config beside `mise.toml`, whose tools, settings, env or hooks mise loads with it
prReviewHighRiskPaths.**/.mise.*.toml: a mise config beside `mise.toml`, whose tools, settings, env or hooks mise loads with it
prReviewHighRiskPaths.**/mise/**: a directory mise reads config from, beside `mise.toml`
prReviewHighRiskPaths.**/.mise/**: a directory mise reads config and pypi locks from, beside `mise.toml`
prReviewHighRiskPaths.**/.config/mise.toml: a mise config beside `mise.toml`, whose tools, settings, env or hooks mise loads with it
prReviewHighRiskPaths.**/.config/mise/**: a directory mise reads config from, beside `mise.toml`
prReviewHighRiskPaths.**/.tool-versions: a version file mise and asdf read, a second home for a pinned tool
prReviewHighRiskPaths..devcontainer/**: the image every container session runs: the mise it copies in, the toolchain it installs, and the hooks' environment
prReviewHighRiskPaths.tools/policy/pr-review.json: the values this reviewer decides by, its own floor among them
prReviewHighRiskPaths.tools/policy/prompt-budgets.json: each prompt's word budget, which rises only with a person's approval
prReviewHighRiskPaths.tools/lib/policy.ts: the loader this reviewer reads its floor through, and the guard its approval label

prReviewHighRiskPathsMeans: The floor, which since D-37 (asdlc-openspec-qcqm, 2026-10-04) is the reviewer's whole decision: a pull request that adds, changes, deletes or renames a file matching one of these globs is high risk, and merges only on a person's approval; the reviewer merges any other. Each key is a glob, matched as `prReviewContextPaths` says, and each value is the reason the review comment gives. Nothing a pull request says raises or lowers it, so none can argue its way past a person into changing CI, this reviewer or the rules. Removing a line lets pull requests that change that file merge without a person, and this key is itself high risk, since its record is on the list. Decided 2026-09-25 (asdlc-openspec-mi6). `tools/policy/pr-review.json` and `tools/policy/prompt-budgets.json` added 2026-10-02 (D-27, asdlc-openspec-umg3), when the keys `prReviewHighRiskJsonKeys` had held to a person key by key moved into those two records whole. `tools/lib/policy.ts` added the same day, by the same change: the reviewer reads this floor through it, so a pull request that changed it alone could change what the floor holds. `.beads/PRIME.md` added 2026-10-03 (asdlc-openspec-z5gy), with the file: the tracker's plugin has `bd prime` print it into every session, as `CLAUDE.md` is loaded into every session, so a pull request that changed it alone could change what every agent is told. `mise.toml` and `mise.lock` added 2026-10-03 (D-31, asdlc-openspec-8juz.2), when they became the one home of the toolchain's versions, which `engines` in `prReviewHighRiskJsonKeys` had partly been. With them, the same day, every other place mise reads a project config from, at any depth, and `.devcontainer/**`, whose image installs the toolchain: a security review found that a config added there would be trusted by CI and the container and read by every shim, and could otherwise merge without a person. On 2026-10-04 D-37 (asdlc-openspec-qcqm) made the floor the whole decision, and its floor lost one path and gained four: `.claude/agents/branch-reviewer.md` replaced `.claude/agents/pr-reviewer.md`, which retired with the model, as the one review of correctness and maintainability left; `scripts/hooks/guard-git.mjs`, the guard on the approval label, came on, since until then only the model's judgement of a weakened guard had held it to a person, with `scripts/hooks/_shared.mjs`, which the guard imports, so the guard cannot be loosened through its helper; and `tools/lib/git-env.ts` came on, since the job that merges imports it beside the loader.
prReviewHighRiskJsonKeysMeans: The second half of the floor: top-level keys of committed JSON files whose value a pull request changes (added, removed or different, compared as parsed JSON) make it high risk. A trailing `*` matches any key with that prefix. It exists because the whole file is too wide: a change to its `scripts` needs no person, and until D-36 (asdlc-openspec-8juz.6) moved every task but `prepare` and `calculator:serve` to `tasks.toml`, most pull requests that added a gate made one. A dependency, an install-script permission or the engine floor does. Decided 2026-09-25 (asdlc-openspec-mi6). Until 2026-10-02 it also held `tools/policy.json` to a person by its `prReview*` keys and, from 2026-09-26 (asdlc-openspec-2wv), its `promptWordBudget*` keys; D-27 (asdlc-openspec-umg3) moved those keys into `tools/policy/pr-review.json` and `tools/policy/prompt-budgets.json`, which `prReviewHighRiskPaths` names whole, and the entry left.
prReviewMergeMethodMeans: How the reviewer merges: the method GitHub's merge endpoint takes. It is `rebase` because `docs/decisions.md` § D-02, item 6, rebase-merges a change's pull request so `mise run worktree:gc` can prove its branch reached the trunk, and the repository allows no other method. Decided 2026-09-25 (asdlc-openspec-mi6).
